intended_object: An injective map from the proper α-colorings of a graph G to its proper β-colorings, which exists whenever |α| ≤ |β| for finite colour sets α, β. You get it by composing each coloring with some injection α ↪ β. This is read off the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The body picks some embedding α ↪ β. One exists because `Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le` turns the hypothesis `card α ≤ card β` into one, and `.some` chooses it. The body then applies `recolorOfEmbedding`, which composes a coloring with the complete-graph embedding induced by α ↪ β, so the result is injective on colorings. That is exactly the docstring's "noncomputable embedding of α-colorings to β-colorings when β has at least as large a cardinality as α".

The finiteness assumption fits the docstring's wording, which compares `Fintype.card`. The arbitrary-embedding version already exists in full generality as `recolorOfEmbedding`. A version stated with cardinals instead of `Fintype.card` would be possible, but this definition is just a convenience wrapper for the finite case, which is the common one for graph colorings, so I do not count it as too narrow. It has no correctness problems.
